facts.text: Local captures exist: `docs/reference/tern-site/` holds 82 Markdown pages (including index.md) with source URLs, byte counts and SHA-256 hashes in `MANIFEST.md`; `docs/reference/tern-sdk/` is pinned to `stencil-hq/tern-sdk` commit 38a4c06.

Research recommendation (not implemented, no live test): build a Pi-side TSP renderer rather than a Tern plugin driving Pi RPC, because `tern.process.run` cannot drive an ongoing JSONL RPC exchange; Pi keeps session state and authorization.

`.pi/lib/tern/tsp.ts` implements TSP v1 encoding (`encodeTsp`), hello+DA1 detection (`helloQuery`, `detectTern`), APC/key input splitting (`splitInput`) and the `TernInlineSurface` class; `run.ts` and `bridge.ts` import it. `encodeTsp` throws above `APC_LIMIT` (65536 bytes) while `encodeTspChunks` splits oversized bodies with `c=<id>` and `m=1`. Live rendering and credit/ack behavior are unverified.

The opt-in Pi-in-Tern runner `.pi/lib/tern/run.ts` (run with `node --experimental-strip-types`) creates a Pi `AgentSessionRuntime` after a TSP probe and binds the Tern UI context via `bridge.uiContext()`, so extension prompts go to native Tern dialogs; it is not default startup. Not run end-to-end in a live pane.

`.pi/lib/tern/run.ts` falls back to spawning `pi` with the original arguments when stdin is not a TTY or probing is disabled (`shouldProbe`), when no TSP hello arrives within `PROBE_MS` (1000 ms), or when DA1 arrives without a TSP hello. It restores raw mode on SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP.

The global `pi` CLI at `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` is v1.1.0, while trebol's `node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` (the SDK the bridge imports) is v1.0.4; `commands.ts` also notes 1.0.4.
